A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FrugalNeRF. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original FrugalNeRF experiments on LLFF, DTU, and RealEstate-10K, including quantitative comparisons and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds loss-source and downsampling ablations, dense-view results, and further geometric comparisons.

M1.justification: The shared multi-scale voxels, reprojection-based depth selection, and training procedure remain unchanged. The optional depth-prior term added to v2's main loss equation was already described in v1 Appendix B.1. Nearest-neighbor downsampling is newly disclosed, without evidence of an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate novel-view synthesis on the same LLFF, DTU, and RealEstate-10K coverage. The added dense-view experiment changes training-view counts within retained coverage. Mentioning 360-degree scenes as a limitation does not establish their evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 adds TensoRF to the corresponding LLFF, DTU, and RealEstate-10K benchmark tables; v1 included it in the training-view-count analysis. Other evaluated comparators are retained. The removed DTU RegNeRF row reported only an out-of-memory failure.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix D.1 adds a dense setting with 17–54 training views beyond v1's 2–16-view analysis. New ablations introduce loss-source and interpolation controls, with rendered-depth-error tracking in Figure 9. Existing benchmark splits, resolutions, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted comparisons of geometric adaptation versus learned depth supervision (Table 5, Figure 9) and nearest-neighbor versus bilinear downsampling (Tables 7–8). It extends the view-count and geometric visualization analyses while retaining the existing scale, component, and scene-dependency studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Added results follow the existing point-estimate and descriptive training-curve reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark averages and per-scene scores are retained. v2 adds TensoRF scores and ablation/dense-view results; Table 6 reports dense-view PSNR of 26.69 for FrugalNeRF versus 26.73 for TensoRF. Table 4 revises the unshared model size from 198.31 to 221.14 MB. The new TensoRF three-view LPIPS entry in Table 13 is malformed as '0.9.11'.

T1.justification: The reprojection derivations and mathematical objectives are substantively retained. Equation reordering, splitting, and explicit inclusion of the previously described optional depth loss introduce no new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain fast, competitive few-shot synthesis through shared multi-scale voxels and geometric adaptation, without requiring learned priors but allowing their integration. The added 'extreme few-shot' wording emphasizes the already evaluated two-to-four-view setting.

C2.justification: v2 attributes learned-depth-only errors to scale mismatch and interprets geometric and learned supervision as complementary. It also motivates nearest-neighbor downsampling through stability and floater suppression, and explicitly names 360-degree scenes in the retained generalization limitation.

D1.justification: v2 first specifies the 0.5 reprojection threshold, loss weights of 0.01, 0.5, and 0.01 for geometric, sparse-depth, and optional depth losses, and nearest-neighbor downsampling. These are additional disclosures. However, Table 1 loses v1's clarification that LLFF evaluation uses full images without visibility masks.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and positioning discussions for DNGaussian and SparseCraft. It revises ReVoRF's treatment and adds an appendix comparison concerning reliability updates and preservation of fine details. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 extensively condenses and rewrites related work, method summaries, experimental discussion, and captions. It reorganizes the appendix, relocates the training-view analysis and depth-prior details, moves limitations after the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The main DTU table becomes a compact two-view table, with the full comparison moved to Appendix Table 13. LLFF RGB/depth material is redistributed across displays, several ablation figures are resized and reordered, and new loss, downsampling, and DTU depth-comparison displays substantially reshape the presentation.

improvement.justification: The added supervision and downsampling ablations provide more direct support for design choices, while explicit thresholds and loss weights improve reproducibility. Dense-view results also clarify performance beyond the principal few-shot setting. These incremental gains outweigh limited reporting drawbacks, including the removed LLFF masking clarification and malformed TensoRF entry in Table 13.
